title: A Heat Transfer Textbook
version: Sixth edition, version 6.00, 19 April 2024, Phlogiston Press. Identified through indexed author-site citation and PDF front matter. No sixth-edition ISBN/DOI verified; the fifth-edition ISBN is deliberately not reused.
pages_equations_tables: Indexed official contents: Chapter 5, transient/multidimensional conduction; section 5.2, lumped-capacity solutions. Chapters not read.
findings: Verified edition-specific lawful textbook lead for heat-transfer fundamentals. Current PDF fetches failed; indexed fragments are not treated as substantive review.
weaknesses_conflicts: Browser returned 502/access failure; workspace download returned 403. No equation or coefficient adopted from unread chapters.
domain: General engineering heat and mass transfer; not an aluminium rolling calibration source.
relevance: P1 thermal model-assumption and verification reading priority; R158 supplies independently accessible teaching derivation now.
provenance: New selection for fundamentals coverage; not recovered from the historical unidentified 14-book list U001.
redistribution: Citations and project-authored analysis only; no source PDF or illustrations committed.

title: Light Alloys: Metallurgy of the Light Metals
version: Fifth edition, 29 March 2017, Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 544 pages; official publisher bibliographic record and contents.
pages_equations_tables: Observed TOC: 2.1 Work Hardening and Annealing; 2.2–2.3 age hardening/ageing; 2.5 Mechanical Behaviour; 4.2 alloy/temper designations; 4.3–4.4 non-heat-treatable/heat-treatable wrought alloys. No chapter text read.
findings: Publisher contents distinguish aluminium physical metallurgy and wrought-alloy families, giving a targeted acquisition syllabus.
weaknesses_conflicts: The publisher description retains an older subtitle while the title heading says Metallurgy of the Light Metals; ISBN and fifth edition pin identity. No constitutive parameters, kinetics or property tables accessed.
domain: Aluminium-specific chapters selected; other chapters cover magnesium, titanium and casting.
relevance: P1 material-card taxonomy and P2 specimen-state provenance; future P3/P4 material and anneal model selection.
provenance: New selection for fundamentals coverage; not recovered from the historical unidentified 14-book list U001.

title: Recrystallization and Related Annealing Phenomena
version: Third edition, 24 July 2017, Elsevier. Publisher shop and indexed ScienceDirect ISBN/edition; no chapter text obtained.
pages_equations_tables: Observed contents: chapters 2–3 deformed state/texture; 6 recovery; 7–9 recrystallization of different material classes; 13 dynamic restoration; 14 continuous recrystallization; measurement appendix.
findings: The contents provide a mechanism-separated reading plan for recovery and annealing research.
weaknesses_conflicts: Official shop TOC jumps from chapter 15 to 18 for computer modelling; numbering is not repaired by guesswork. This third edition must not be attributed to the earlier Humphreys–Hatherly edition. No kinetics constants obtained.
domain: General physical metallurgy across material classes; aluminium applicability needs chapter-level verification.
relevance: P1 explicit non-capability labels for annealing; P2 treatment-state documentation; future P4 model and measurement selection.

title: Recovery and Recrystallization: Phenomena, Physics, Models, Simulation
version: Published chapter 23, Physical Metallurgy, fifth edition, editors David E. Laughlin and Kazuhiro Hono, Elsevier 2014, pp.2291–2397; author-hosted personal copy, 108 PDF pages. Publisher book date 23 July 2014.
findings: Recovery reorganizes stored defects; JMAK assumptions restrict a fitted isothermal law. Statistical texture models omit local topology; cellular automata require calibrated physical time and length scales.
weaknesses_conflicts: Selected sections, not the entire chapter or book, reviewed. General mechanisms and examples include aluminium and steel; no steel constants transfer to aluminium. Review synthesis is not new plant data.
domain: General metallic recovery/recrystallization with explicitly identified aluminium examples.
relevance: P1 state semantics; P2 supplied treatment versus predicted evolution; P4 anneal identifiability and fidelity decision.
provenance: New selection for fundamentals coverage; not recovered from the historical unidentified 14-book list U001.
redistribution: Citations and project-authored analysis only; no source PDF or illustrations committed.

title: Part 3: Introduction to Engineering Heat Transfer, MIT 16.050 Thermal Energy
authors: MIT OpenCourseWare; course instructor Zoltan Spakovszky
version: Fall 2002 course notes, Part 3, 74-page institutional PDF. Course attribution verified; individual section authorship not separately asserted. Not a commercial textbook or Lienhard edition.
findings: Derives series conduction/convection resistance and the lumped cooling energy balance, with a small-Biot-number approximation and exponential constant-property limit.
weaknesses_conflicts: Aerospace/general teaching examples do not calibrate roll-strip conductance or coolant coefficients. A fixed-temperature reservoir solution is not the exact finite-capacity two-body contact solution.
domain: General continuum heat transfer; no aluminium-specific property validation.
relevance: P1 dimensional, equilibrium-limit and timestep verification; P2 reject thermal validation claims from force-only evidence.
provenance: New selection for fundamentals coverage; not recovered from the historical unidentified 14-book list U001.
redistribution: Citations and project-authored analysis only; no source PDF or illustrations committed.
